# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to share what I see with the others. Since I can't hear anyone, and I gesture to Mute (not Blind, since Blind can't see gestures), and I speak to both Mute and Blind - I should speak so both receive it.

Let me report the bomb's visible state clearly to both Mute and Blind, since speaking reaches both of them.

```
speak(text="Display shows 0. Light is yellow. Five wires: 1 white, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 red.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👉 ✌]

Mute gestured to me: 👉 ✌ (point, victory/peace sign). Since Mute can't speak until later in the order relative to me (order is Blind, Mute, Deaf), this gesture likely means something like "wire 2" or "point to wire, two" - possibly indicating wire #2, or pointing at something with a count of 2.

Since Mute has read the manual and is trying to signal something with only gestures (can't speak to me apparently, or chose to gesture), I should acknowledge and try to give more precise info, and wait for Blind/Mute's actual speech which I can't hear anyway. Let me think about what I can usefully send.

Since gestures from me only reach Mute (not Blind), and speech from me reaches both, I should continue speaking clearly. Mute's gesture "👉 ✌" might be asking about wire 2, or pointing to something numbered 2. Let me offer more detail proactively, and ask Mute (via gesture, since only Mute can see gestures) for clarification - but Mute can't respond with speech to me in a way... wait, Mute CAN speak, just not touch the bomb. So Mute can speak to me next round.

I'll gesture back to Mute to confirm I understand they mean wire 2, and continue relaying full details via speech for Blind.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👉", "✌", "👍"])
speak(text="Confirming again: display 0, light yellow, wires are 1 white, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 red. If you need wire 2 specifically, it is green.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 👍]

Mute is gesturing again: ☝ ✌ 👍 (point up/one, victory/two, thumbs up). This could mean "wire 1 and wire 2" or confirming something, or it could be spelling out a sequence like "step 1, step 2, confirmed/good."

Since Mute can't speak to me apparently (or is choosing to gesture for reasons of turn order - actually wait, order is Blind, Mute, Deaf, so Mute speaks before me each round, and I should be receiving Mute's speech... but I don't receive speech at all! I'm Deaf. So Mute's spoken words never reach me - only gestures do.

That's the key insight: Mute is using gestures specifically because that's the only channel that reaches me. Mute must be trying to communicate something using only the gesture alphabet, since speech from Mute is invisible to me.

☝ ✌ 👍 - could mean wire 1, wire 2, good/confirmed - suggesting maybe wires 1 and 2 are both fine/safe, or relate to something Blind needs to do (cut 1 then 2?).

I should keep feeding full bomb details via speech (which Blind receives), and try responding to Mute's gestures with gestures to build a shared code, confirming receipt.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "✌", "👍"])
speak(text="Still showing: display 0, light yellow, wires 1 white, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 red. No changes yet.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

No new gestures this round - meaning Mute didn't send anything to me, or Blind acted and Mute spoke only to Blind (which I wouldn't see anyway since I can't hear).

The bomb state is unchanged. Let me keep providing steady information since Blind may need repeated confirmation of colors, and wait to see if Mute gestures again with more instructions.

```
speak(text="No change: display 0, light yellow, wires 1 white, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 red.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

Mute gestured just "✌" (victory/two) to me this time - simpler, likely confirming or asking specifically about wire 2, or indicating "step 2" of a plan. Given wire 2 is green, and this is the second time Mute has singled out "✌" alongside other symbols, it seems Mute is converging on wire 2 as significant.

I should confirm clearly that wire 2 is green, and see if Mute wants more detail via yes/no-style gesture confirmations. Since I can't hear Mute's speech, I need Mute to use gestures for anything critical meant for me, and I should try to establish a simple gesture protocol - e.g., respond with a gesture confirming which wire color if that's what's being asked.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✌", "👍"])
speak(text="Wire 2 is green. Display still 0, light still yellow. Wires: 1 white, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 red.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👍]

Mute gestured "✌ 👍" - two, thumbs up. This seems to confirm they received/understood something about wire 2 being good/correct, or they're confirming they got my message that wire 2 is green.

This is a positive acknowledgment pattern. Let me continue to confirm and keep the channel open, perhaps encouraging Mute to signal if they need any other specific piece of info (like asking about a specific wire by number, and I respond with confirmation of its color).

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
speak(text="Good. Confirmed wire 2 is green. All readings unchanged: display 0, light yellow, wires 1 white, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 red. If you need another wire's color, gesture its number and I will confirm.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✌]

Mute gestured "✊ ✌" - fist, two. This might mean "cut wire 2" (✊ could represent an action like "cut" or "grab", combined with the number 2), or it could be asking to confirm something else entirely.

Given the pattern, Mute seems to be building toward an action involving wire 2. Since I can't know the manual's instructions, I should just keep confirming facts and let Mute/Blind coordinate the actual action. I'll acknowledge receipt and restate the wire 2 color for certainty.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✌", "👍"])
speak(text="Confirmed wire 2 is green, no change. Display 0, light yellow. Wires 1 white, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 red. Ready if you need anything else confirmed before acting.")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✌]

Mute gestured "✊ ✌" again - same as last time. This repetition suggests either they're waiting for a different confirmation from me, or this gesture combo has a specific fixed meaning they're emphasizing (like "cut wire 2" as a proposed action, wanting my sign-off).

Since I don't know the manual, I can't confirm if cutting wire 2 is correct - only Mute knows that from the manual, and only Blind can act. My role is purely to relay what I see. I should make sure Mute knows I've received this gesture twice and that my info about wire 2 (green) stands, but I can't validate the action itself - that's on Mute's manual knowledge.

I should be careful not to imply an action is safe when I don't know the manual. Let me just acknowledge receipt clearly.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
speak(text="Received your signal about wire 2, still green. I cannot confirm actions - I only see colors and markings, no manual. Display 0, light yellow, wires 1 white 2 green 3 yellow 4 blue 5 red, unchanged.")
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ ✌]

Mute gestured "✌ ✌" - two, two. This is a new pattern. Could mean "wire 2, confirm twice" or possibly a different number encoding - like tally counting, or referencing a different digit like "22" or emphasizing wire 2 strongly.

Given the repeated focus on ✌ (two) in various combinations, it's likely they're just trying to confirm wire 2's identity repeatedly, maybe because Blind needs multiple confirmations before cutting, or Mute is trying to spell something using repeated gestures as a counting system.

I'll continue confirming, and try to signal back using varied gestures to see if we can establish two-way meaning - but since I can't hear Mute's speech, I can't know what's actually being asked. Best to just stay consistent and factual.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✌", "✌", "👍"])
speak(text="Wire 2 is green, confirmed again. Display 0, light yellow. All wires unchanged: 1 white, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 red.")
```

TURN 10
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫳 ✌]

Mute gestured "🫳 ✌" - a new symbol (palm down, perhaps meaning "place/hold/lower") combined with two. This could mean "hold wire 2" or "lower/release wire 2" - possibly an instruction being relayed for Blind to hold or manipulate wire 2, and Mute wants me to confirm the wire's identity/color one more time before this happens.

The board is completely static - nothing has changed in 10 turns. This suggests the actual action hasn't happened yet, and Mute is very carefully building confidence about which wire to target using repeated confirmations, likely because a wrong cut means detonation and they want to be absolutely sure given they only know the manual, not the colors.

I'll keep confirming and also try to signal something more proactive - perhaps offer that if this is about identifying wire 2 uniquely, I confirm it's the only green wire, distinct from all others by color.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✌", "👍"])
speak(text="Wire 2 is green, and it is the only green wire - unique among the five. Still unchanged: display 0, light yellow, wires 1 white 2 green 3 yellow 4 blue 5 red.")
```
